summary: This skill drives the Nansen CLI (`nansen`, installed from the npm package nansen-cli) to quote and execute Solana/Base DEX swaps, cross-chain bridges, Solana limit orders and Hyperliquid perpetual orders. It needs the `nansen` binary, a Nansen wallet holding EVM and Solana keys, the wallet password (NANSEN_WALLET_PASSWORD, persisted in ~/.nansen/.env), and a Nansen API key or browser session (NANSEN_API_KEY). It also uses the optional NANSEN_YES and NANSEN_REQUIRE_CONFIRM variables. The CLI talks to the Nansen API (compliance screening, price search, hosted simulation), Hyperliquid and chain RPCs, and non-interactive agent runs sign irreversible trades without a prompt unless the operator sets NANSEN_REQUIRE_CONFIRM=1.

findings.message: NANSEN_API_KEY is only named as primaryEnv, not listed under requires.env, yet it takes precedence for all Nansen API calls (lines 43 and 232).
NANSEN_YES and NANSEN_REQUIRE_CONFIRM are read by the CLI to skip or force confirmation of trades but are not declared in requires.env.
NANSEN_WALLET_PASSWORD, the password that unlocks the signing wallet, is required for trade execute and persisted in plaintext ~/.nansen/.env, which the agent is told to source before executing.
The agent is instructed to generate and persist a wallet password to disk via the nansen-wallet-manager skill if none is present, so it creates a signing credential on its own.
The skill has the agent run `nansen wallet create` (line 55); this wallet stores both EVM and Solana keys that are used to sign swaps, bridges and perp orders.
trade quote and execute send the signing and destination wallet addresses to the Nansen API for compliance screening before quoting or signing.
Hosted simulation sends the selected Nansen credential to the Nansen API origin, and perp commands (line 247) submit signed orders to Hyperliquid.
When stdin is not a terminal, as in an agent shell, trade execute broadcasts irreversible transactions without a prompt (same for perp at line 268) unless the operator sets NANSEN_REQUIRE_CONFIRM=1.
The install spec fetches the npm package nansen-cli, and allowed-tools (line 39) grants Bash(nansen:*), so the package's code runs with wallet-signing capability.
The change log says skill-card.md was removed, yet skill-card.md ships in this release, so the listing and the files disagree.
